title: Minister defends 2027 permanent residency plan, says 'vast majority' are already in Canada
summary: Immigration Minister Lena Diab says the federal government is managing newcomers responsibly as the Conservative Opposition seeks to block a plan that could see as many as 662,000 people receive…

image.caption: Minister of Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Lena Metlege Diab says a one-time measure will add a maximum of 200,000 permanent residents above federal targets. Her office said most of those people are already in Canada. (Keito Newman/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: Immigration Minister Lena Diab says the federal government is managing newcomers responsibly as the Conservative Opposition seeks to block a plan that could see as many as 662,000 people receive permanent residency next year.
Conservative motion seeks to block government's plan
Ottawa has an annual target of 380,000 permanent resident admissions for the next three years. But up to 282,000 additional permanent admissions are planned through one-time measures in 2027.
Diab's office says the "vast majority of these admissions will be transitioning people who are already in Canada to permanent residence."
As part of that total, Diab says 100,000 slots are for workers who will be nominated by provinces and territories, and those slots will go unfilled if those governments decide they don't need them.

blocks.text: Conservative immigration critic Michelle Rempel Garner argues Canada can't absorb all of those people without putting additional strains on the housing and job markets and social infrastructure.
An Opposition motion being debated on Parliament Hill on Tuesday calls to block the government's permanent residency plan
The Bloc Québécois says it plans to support the Conservative motion, which cannot pass without the support of some members of the Liberal majority government.
With files from The Canadian Press
